Today app/leer/scene-page.tsx derives figure placement itself: `figsByN` (group `pic.figures` by `endN`), the "a figure for n lands after its last visible fragment" rule (`arr[i + 1]?.n !== p.n`), `pageOf(n)` (index of the sub-page holding paragraph ordinal n, -1 if none) and `gotoFigure` (page jump + scroll + pulse). One concept is split across the hook and the caller and none of it is tested.
- Create a pure, framework-free module next to use-pictures.ts (e.g. app/folio/figure-placement.ts) with small exported functions, e.g. `groupFiguresByEndN(figures)`, `figuresAfter(paragraphs, i, grouped)` (returns the figures to render after paragraph i of the visible sub-page: only when it is the last visible fragment of its ordinal), and `pageOfOrdinal(pages, n)`. Use them from scene-page.tsx. The DOM side of gotoFigure (setPage, scroll, double rAF, pulse) may stay in scene-page.tsx but must call `pageOfOrdinal`.
- Vitest tests (app/folio/figure-placement.test.ts): grouping keeps insertion order per endN; a paragraph split across fragments (same n, later ones `cont`) gets its figures only after the last fragment on that page; when a paragraph's fragments span two pages, figures render only on the page with its last visible fragment there (document the current behavior exactly as the existing code does it, do not change it); several figures on one paragraph; no figures; `pageOfOrdinal` found, on a later page, and -1 for missing.

## 2. Make the hook's implicit ordering rules explicit and tested; trim its surface where safe
use-pictures.ts returns 14 fields with silent rules: one `busyRef` gates scene AND figure requests (a second request while one is in flight is a silent no-op), `retryFigure` only works from the `error` phase, and the caller threads `pref` into three calls.
- Extract the rules into pure exported functions in the same new module (or a sibling), e.g. a tiny request gate (`tryStart`/`finish` over a plain object, or `canStart(busy)`), `canRetryFigure(figure)` (true only for phase "error"), and `canIllustrateScene({ sceneId, busy, cached })`. Use them in the hook. Test them: scene in flight blocks a figure and vice versa; finish releases; retry refused from loading/ready, allowed from error; scene refused when cached or no sceneId.
- Add a short doc comment at the top of use-pictures.ts listing the ordering rules (one request at a time across scene+figure; retry only from error; caller must call hidePopover on pager moves).
- Simplify the surface only where it is clearly safe and behavior-neutral: take `pref` as a hook argument (`usePictures({ bookId, textVersion, sceneId, pref })`, read through a ref so callbacks stay stable) so `illustrateScene()`, `illustratePassage()`, `retryFigure(id)` no longer take `pref`; group the lightbox trio as `lightbox: { item, open, close }` if that is a clean change across callers. Update every caller (grep: scene-page.tsx, panels-modal.tsx, vault.tsx, image-pane.tsx, inline-figures.tsx, anything else). Do not change anything else in the hook's behavior.

## 3. Single-source picture copy, icon and theme key
- `PictureIcon` SVG is duplicated in app/folio/image-pane.tsx and app/folio/inline-figures.tsx; `Sketching…`, `Try again` and `Remove picture` (aria-label and title) appear in both. Move the icon and these strings into one small shared module (e.g. app/folio/picture-copy.tsx exporting `PictureIcon` and a `PICTURE_COPY` const) and use it in both views. Strings must stay byte-identical. If app/folio/copy-gates.test.ts asserts copy, keep it passing and extend it if natural. Never use the word "Generated" in any UI copy.
- Theme key: `THEME_KEY = "lectoria.theme"` lives in app/folio/chrome.tsx while app/theme.ts hand-writes the same literal inside `THEME_SCRIPT` (inlined by app/layout.tsx). Move `THEME_KEY` into app/theme.ts, build `THEME_SCRIPT` by interpolating it (use JSON.stringify(THEME_KEY) inside the template), and re-export or update imports so app/folio/chrome.tsx and app/reader.tsx keep working (prefer re-exporting from chrome.tsx so reader.tsx needs no edit). Keep the default LIGHT behavior exactly. Extend app/theme.test.ts: the script contains JSON.stringify(THEME_KEY); evaluating THEME_SCRIPT with a fake localStorage/document (null, "garbage", "dark", "light", and a throwing localStorage) sets data-theme to light/light/dark/light/light.

## Done when
`npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, `npm run check:isolation`, `npm run check:size`, `npm run check:secrets`, `npm run test:hooks` all pass. Write a short docs/tasks/32-pictures-placement.md (what and why), update the relevant docs/contracts/*.md line only if a documented interface changed, add a row to BUILT_DURING_HACKATHON.md in the existing format. Commit in 2-3 focused commits. Do not push.

85|
86|Owner decisions. Short and binding.
87|
88|- Desktop first. No mobile or iOS work now.
89|- The reader shows one scene at a time. Sub-pages split long scenes by length only. Music cues run on scene entry.
90|- A chapter holds several scenes. Each scene has its own emotion.
91|- Paragraph ids carry a global ordinal `n`. Compare `n`, never id strings.
92|- `book.json` is frozen with a `textVersion` hash. Every cache key includes it.
93|- Scenes cover each chapter's paragraphs with no gaps and no overlaps. No scene crosses a chapter boundary. Scenes split at strong sequential emotion shifts; blends stay in the vector.
94|- Emotions are distributions. Each scene stores the full Jev probability vector over the 8 ids, plus `intensity` (0 to 1) and `tempo` (energy, 0 to 1). The Muse override on low confidence edits the vector and records that it did. It never swaps in a single label.
95|- Music is about 15 tracks, pre-generated offline with MusicGen on Modal as one coherent soundtrack: same orchestra and instrumentation, same leitmotif style. 96|- The player picks the track nearest to the scene vector, by cosine similarity over the vector plus intensity and tempo. Hysteresis stops it from flipping on small changes. Skip or change track overrides until the next scene.
97|- The owner listens to short clips before any full generation. Agents do not run Modal until the owner says so.

104|- Spend is counted in integer micro-dollars. Reserve with Redis `INCRBY` before each model call and refund with `DECRBY` after. Reserve per call, including retries.
105|- The server clamps every model tool argument. Tool arguments are untrusted input.
106|- The CSP allows `challenges.cloudflare.com` (script and frame) and `*.public.blob.vercel-storage.com` (images).
107|- The "Picture this" cache key is the book plus the paragraph where the selection starts plus `textVersion` plus `promptVersion`. Never generate the same image twice for one paragraph. The prompt is built from that paragraph plus scene context.
108|- The "Picture scene" cache key is the book plus the scene id plus `textVersion` plus `promptVersion`.
109|- Images live in Vercel Blob at deterministic public paths (`addRandomSuffix: false`, `allowOverwrite: false`). Routes return Blob URLs, never image bytes.
110|- Modal endpoints require proxy auth. Tokens live only in env.
111|
112|## Security rules
113|
114|Summary. The full rules live in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).
115|
116|- Secrets live only in env vars: `.env.local` locally (gitignored), Vercel env vars in prod.
117|- `.env.example` holds names only, never values.
118|- Never use a `NEXT_PUBLIC_` variable for a secret. Only public ids such as the Turnstile site key may use it.
119|- `core/` stays pure: no keys, no env reads, no network clients, no `server-only`. 120|- The pre-commit secret scan must pass. Never bypass it with `--no-verify`.
121|- Errors to the client are generic. Details go to server logs only, never with keys.
122|- Never log request headers.
123|
124|## Writing rules
125|
126|Run docs, UI copy, and commit messages through the `unslop` skill: no filler, no hype, no emoji in headings, none of seamless, elevate, delve, robust, leverage. Headings use sentence case. Commit messages use an imperative subject under 72 chars, and the body says why.
127|
128|## Design
129|
130|Minimalist, functional, elegant. No generic AI-template look: no purple or violet anywhere, no gradient blobs, no glassmorphism, no emoji icons, no stock hero sections.
131|
132|The palette comes from Meta's brand. Meta blue `#0866FF` is the single accent, `#0064E0` for hover and pressed states. Text is near-black `#1C2B33`. Surfaces are white `#FFFFFF` and soft gray `#F1F4F7`. Dark mode keeps the same accent on a near-black surface: `#0B1215` surface, `#E4E6EB` text.
133|
134|The layout is typography-first. The book sits centered with a comfortable measure, about 60 to 70 chars per line. The companion chat lives in a quiet side panel. Whitespace is generous, the accent color is single, motion is subtle: under 200 ms, and it respects `prefers-reduced-motion`.
135|
136|These values live as CSS custom properties in [app/tokens.css](app/tokens.css), which is the source of truth.
137|
138|## Hooks
139|
140|`npm install` (or `npm run prepare`) points `core.hooksPath` at `.githooks`. The `pre-commit` hook rejects staged files over 5000 tokens and staged secrets. 106|- The CSP allows `challenges.cloudflare.com` (script and frame) and `*.public.blob.vercel-storage.com` (images).
107|- The "Picture this" cache key is the book plus the paragraph where the selection starts plus `textVersion` plus `promptVersion`. Never generate the same image twice for one paragraph. The prompt is built from that paragraph plus scene context.

122|- Never log request headers.

125|
126|Run docs, UI copy, and commit messages through the `unslop` skill: no filler, no hype, no emoji in headings, none of seamless, elevate, delve, robust, leverage. Headings use sentence case. Commit messages use an imperative subject under 72 chars, and the body says why.

128|## Design
129|
130|Minimalist, functional, elegant. No generic AI-template look: no purple or violet anywhere, no gradient blobs, no glassmorphism, no emoji icons, no stock hero sections.
131|
132|The palette comes from Meta's brand. Meta blue `#0866FF` is the single accent, `#0064E0` for hover and pressed states. Text is near-black `#1C2B33`. Surfaces are white `#FFFFFF` and soft gray `#F1F4F7`. Dark mode keeps the same accent on a near-black surface: `#0B1215` surface, `#E4E6EB` text.
133|
